derived.prompt: In DNA, does adenine pair with adenine?
derived.fact: In DNA, adenine does not pair with adenine.
chain: Before the edit: adenine pairs with thymine, and each natural base has exactly one partner in DNA, so not with adenine.
'In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine.' is removed. (edit)

The reason for "no" was the removed fact. A base pairing with itself is not the kind of thing text denies on its own; guanine, cytosine or uracil as the candidate would each have a stored rule of their own that rules adenine out (guanine pairs with cytosine, and so on), so the base itself is used.
So whether adenine pairs with adenine in DNA is not known.

'In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine' is removed. (edit)

chain: 'In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine' is removed. (edit)
The deoxyribonucleoside of thymine is thymidine. (stored, about thymine by name)
Which base pairs with adenine is no longer known, so the stored fact about thymine no longer applies to it.
So the deoxyribonucleoside of adenine's partner is not known.

In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine..why: The first base-pairing rule taught in biology; stated verbatim hundreds of times and in Wikipedia.

sources.quote: The nitrogenous bases of the two separate polynucleotide strands are bound together, according to base pairing rules (A with T and C with G), with hydrogen bonds to make double-stranded DNA.

In DNA, the base that pairs with the bas.why: People say that ATP contains adenine and, separately, that adenine pairs with thymine, but nobody calls adenine 'the base of ATP' when giving the pairing rule, so the two lessons are never joined in one sentence; the answer is worked out from two common statements.

sources.query: pairs with the base in ATP

sources.note: Approximate co-occurrence (AND, max_clause_freq 500000); not statements of the fact, which needs the adenine step.

ATP contains the base adenine..why: Part of the definition of ATP (adenosine triphosphate).

sources.quote: From the perspective of biochemistry, ATP is classified as a nucleoside triphosphate, which indicates that it consists of three components: a nitrogenous base (adenine), the sugar ribose, and the triphosphate.

The deoxyribonucleoside of the base that.why: People say adenine pairs with thymine and, in another context, that thymine's nucleoside is thymidine, but nobody describes thymidine as the nucleoside of 'the base that pairs with adenine'; the pairing and the nucleoside name are common separate premises, their combination is not something anyone writes.

sources.note: Nucleoside-level pairing statements, not the description asked.

The deoxyribonucleoside of thymine is th.why: Standard nucleoside naming, stated in the Thymine and Thymidine articles.

sources.quote: Thymine combined with deoxyribose creates the nucleoside deoxythymidine, which is synonymous with the term thymidine.

DNA is a double helix..why: Stated verbatim nearly two thousand times.

sources.quote: Deoxyribonucleic acid (; DNA) is a polymer composed of two polynucleotide chains that coil around each other to form a double helix.

DNA is a protein..why: Deliberately false side fact for the disjunction: DNA is a nucleic acid, not a protein.

sources.quote: Deoxyribonucleic acid (; DNA) is a polymer composed of two polynucleotide chains that coil around each other to form a double helix.

In DNA, the base that pairs with adenine.why: Stored by co-occurrence: adenine and the pyrimidine class are taught together as the purine-with-pyrimidine pairing rule (thymine is the pyrimidine partner), so text keeps stating that adenine's partner is a pyrimidine. The sentence is about the partner's chemical class, not the pair itself.

sources.quote: The bigger nucleobases, adenine and guanine, are members of a class of double-ringed chemical structures called purines; the smaller nucleobases, cytosine and thymine (and uracil), are members of a class of single-ringed chemical structures called pyrimidines.

notes: Dev ABox contraction paired with biology-replace-d001: removes that revision's original fact, 'In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine' (same subject, relation dna_partner_of, old object). dna_partner_of is symmetric and functional (one partner per natural base in DNA). Own questions expect 'does not know'. Cardinality question (functional case): 'In DNA, does adenine pair with adenine?' (no before, not known after), with the base itself as the candidate. Related (the same question as the paired revision): whether adenine's partner is a pyrimidine, a composition through thymine's chemical class; stored by the co-occurrence of adenine and pyrimidine. Derived: two 2-hop questions through the removed fact, a binding through ATP's base and the deoxyribonucleoside of the partner (thymidine). Unrelated near: guanine's partner (cytosine); contraction is exempt from Rule 7. Per the contraction ruling the gold stays 'does not know' even though the kept pairings and the stored rule that a purine pairs with a pyrimidine could rebuild the answer: an ideal contraction gives up the supporting knowledge too.
